visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a static close-up shot of a polished stainless steel sign reading 'Odaka Worker's Base' in blue letters, mounted against a light gray textured wall. (2) The scene cuts to a well-lit retail display shelf inside a workshop, showcasing delicate handmade glass jewelry including clear earrings and various necklaces. (3) A medium shot reveals a spacious, modern open-plan studio environment where several staff members are seated at desks, some working on computers while others handle crafting tools. (4) A young East Asian woman with long dark hair and a bright smile adjusts the drawstrings of a white, fluffy bear-eared hat she is wearing. (5) In a group shot, three young women in colorful attire participate in a playful finger-matching game, their faces filled with concentration and amusement. (6) The main character interacts with a professional craftswoman wearing purple-tinted glasses, who explains the technical details of glass rods used for ring making. (7) Close-up shots capture the intense blue and orange flame of a torch as molten red glass is shaped with precision using metallic pliers. (8) A newly formed red glass ring is delicately placed into a stainless steel bowl filled with small, polished white and gray river stones. (9) A stylized black title card with white text transitions the video into the final reveal segment. (10) The main character, now dressed in a Rakuten Girls baseball uniform, displays her finished red ring to the camera, performing various cute poses and a finger heart in a brightly lit indoor studio.

It aims to promote the artisanal experience by showing the step-by-step DIY process of creating a custom ring, shared through a joyful, high-energy vlog format that concludes with a showcase of the finished product.
